goal: Provide a deterministic, bounded, read-only implementation-context handoff from an explicitly selected plan task or batch and its verified spec.
architecture: Define the portable result schema in agent-plugins first, then vendor and validate it in wisp-schema. Put result and Rust error types in wisp-model, direct bounded selected-chain reads and validation in wisp-artifacts, and JSON error adaptation in wisp-cli; do not route this operation through whole-graph discovery or Git status.

tasks.title: Define the portable implementation-context contract upstream
steps: Add a closed implementation-context@1 JSON Schema with distinct success and error envelopes, stable error codes, exact selected task/criterion projection, source schema IDs and SHA-256 digests, output limit, checks, and gaps.
Keep the schema independent of Rust private types and do not add a harness consumer or runtime_files reference in this task.
Validate the schema JSON and run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`; expect the upstream repository checks to pass.
Commit the schema in agent-plugins before copying it so Wisp can record an immutable source revision and byte digest.

tasks.title: Vendor and register implementation-context@1
steps: Copy the authored agent-plugins schema byte-for-byte. Record its immutable source revision and digest after the upstream schema change is committed; while it is staged only, mark provenance pending and block consumer/release integration.
Embed the result schema and add a dedicated output-contract validator; keep this transient response separate from Contract's canonical artifact types and directories.
Add success and error envelope fixtures and tests that validate both against the pinned schema and check the provenance digest.
Run `cargo test --offline --locked -p wisp-schema`; expect all contract registry tests to pass.

tasks.title: Assemble the selected plan/spec context without graph or Git scans
steps: Add ImplementationSelection with a selector kind and ID, ImplementationContext, and a Rust-native ImplementationContextError aligned with implementation-context@1 while keeping wisp-model independent of other Wisp crates.

Expose `assemble_implementation_context(workspace: &Utf8Path, plan_path: &Utf8Path, selection: ImplementationSelection, output_limit_bytes: usize) -> Result<ImplementationContext, ImplementationContextError>` from wisp-artifacts.

Implement a separate selected-chain operation; safely resolve and read only the explicit plan and its declared spec, validate both pinned schemas, identity/path/hash links, uniqueness, task selection, criterion mappings, and declared dependency references.
Preserve source ordering and exact selected task/criterion fields, report absent modify/test targets as gaps, and never infer dependency completion or execute plan steps.
Canonicalize paths beneath the workspace before reading; reject traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, unsupported hash forms, and inconsistent inputs with typed failures.
Re-read plan/spec bytes before returning; if observed bytes differ, discard the context and return inputs_changed. Do not call discover_graph, assemble_context, or Git status.
Read each plan/spec source through an inclusive 1,048,576-byte cap before parsing; apply the same cap to stability rereads and return budget_exceeded when exceeded.
Use a private test seam for a deterministic plan/spec edit between the initial reads and final stability check; verify inputs_changed rather than relying on a timing race.

Add temporary-workspace tests for valid selection, link/hash/identity failures, duplicate/missing references, unsafe paths, symlink escape, missing targets, unrelated invalid artifacts, and unchanged inputs/Git status/derived state.
Run `cargo test --offline --locked -p wisp-model -p wisp-artifacts`; expect the focused model and artifact tests to pass.

tasks.title: Expose the bounded implementation brief command
steps: Add `wisp brief implement` with explicit workspace and plan arguments and mutually exclusive required batch/task selectors.

Use a 32,768-byte default successful-output limit; enforce the inclusive 256-byte minimum and 1,048,576-byte maximum for --max-bytes, counting the terminating newline and never truncating required context.

Adapt the Rust-native library error to the pinned implementation-context@1 envelope at the CLI boundary; in JSON mode write one document to stdout and return a nonzero exit for every failure without serializing partial context.

Add real-binary tests for task selection, repeated/missing/contradictory selectors, output limits, schema-valid JSON, exit status, and stdout/stderr separation; retain library fixtures for path, link, schema, drift, and stability errors.
Run `cargo test --offline --locked -p wisp-cli --test cli`; expect all CLI integration tests to pass.

tasks.title: Document the handoff boundary and verify the workspace
steps: Update the architecture model after the live result abstraction exists; document that this selected-chain operation does not use whole-graph discovery or Git status.

Update README and architecture/MVP docs to describe the implemented Wisp core, input bounds, platform coverage, API/wire boundary, and separately state that controlled value evaluation remains pending.
Run `just ci`; expect format check, locked workspace tests, strict Clippy, rustdoc warnings, and cargo-deny to pass. Record any non-failing duplicate-version warnings without suppressing them.

tasks.title: Add optional Claude/AGY and Codex consumers with native fallback

test: agent-plugins checkout: consumer contract tests and repository checks
real Wisp CLI against an explicit selected-plan success; Wisp CLI failure tests

steps: Keep Wisp optional. Invoke it only when an explicit persisted plan path and exactly one declared batch or task selection are available; do not infer either value.

Consume only a successful implementation-context@1 result for the requested selection. Treat it as exact artifact context, never as approval, current-code evidence, dependency completion, or permission to execute plan commands.

On Wisp absence, execution failure, unsupported/malformed output, or a rejected input chain, return to the existing native artifact workflow without changing its policy. In particular, retain Claude/AGY warning-and-gap behavior and Codex stop-on-drift behavior.
Review native Claude/AGY and Codex counterparts; load the result schema in Codex runtime_files, update Smith release metadata consistently, and regenerate rather than edit generated Codex files.

Add repository tests that guard both authored skill contracts, untrusted free-text handling, distinct native drift behavior, and Codex schema packaging; exercise a successful explicit selection with the real Wisp CLI. Keep model-level behavior and task outcomes in the later value experiment. Do not add hooks, automatic command execution, or a mandatory Wisp dependency.
Run the agent-plugins repository checks and record the cross-harness change classification.
tasks.commit_message: feat(smith): consume optional Wisp implementation context
